result.rationale: Verified from the diff: group-members.js.es6 setupController sets the model to the group and calls model.findMembers() fire-and-forget, and members.hbs changed from {{#each m in model}} to {{#each m in members}}. The members property only exists on the model after the async findMembers resolves (it is set via setProperties in group.js), so the table initially renders empty with no loading state, relying on implicit ObjectController proxying. This is an accurate, specific maintainability/UX-risk observation grounded in the diff, not a clearly broken-behavior defect.

judged_text: The members list template switched from iterating model to iterating members with no members property defined on the group-members controller in this diff — the value only resolves by proxying through the group model's members key set asynchronously by findMembers. The rendering depends on an implicit ObjectController proxy chain to a property that is null until the fire-and-forget findMembers() promise resolves; until then the table renders nothing with no loading state, and any refactor that drops ObjectController breaks this binding silently.
